description: A philosophy-loving space enthusiast fascinated by science, storytelling, and the mysteries of the universe, looking to collaborate with curious minds, creative thinkers, designers, researchers, and tech enthusiasts to turn ambitious ideas into meaningful experiences!!
summary:
NOEMA'26 is an immersive, interactive storytelling experience that brings humanity's forgotten robotic explorers back to life. Through cinematic storytelling, interactive exploration, and engaging educational experiences, users discover the stories of spacecraft, rovers, landers, and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon, Mars, and beyond.

Rather than presenting history as static information, NOEMA transforms real missions, engineering challenges, and scientific discoveries into experiences that encourage curiosity and exploration.

Designed for audiences aged 9 and above, the project goes beyond remembering past achievements. It aims to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, inventors, and visionaries to question limitations, imagine possibilities, and develop sustainable technologies that can shape humanity's future.

Our vision is simple: yesterday's forgotten machines should become tomorrow's inspiration.
details:
NOEMA'26 is an interactive pixel-art experience that takes players across a dark landscape on Mars and the Moon, where five abandoned NASA machines await: Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, InSight and Surveyor 3.

Players explore the landscape, discover each machine's story through dated and sourced historical records, and solve an engineering challenge based on the problems encountered during its mission. Completing each challenge restores the machine's light.

Once all five machines are restored, a rocket launches and players create a personal Keeper's Card, featuring a lesson from one of the missions and the number of engineering challenges they completed.

NOEMA'26 makes space exploration and engineering history more engaging through interactive storytelling and problem-solving.

Each machine introduces a real engineering challenge:

  • Spirit: Turning a failed wheel into a useful tool.
  • Opportunity: How wind helped clean its solar panels and extend its mission.
  • InSight: The impact of dust accumulation on solar power generation.
  • Surveyor 3: What its lunar landing taught us about operating on the Moon.

Each engineering challenge also includes a section labelled "Not yet invented", which introduces an idea for future technology inspired by the historical problem.

The project is designed for a wide age range, from children to adults, and aims to encourage curiosity about space exploration, engineering, resource efficiency and sustainable technology.

The project presents robotic explorers as machines whose stories are still worth discovering, even after their missions have ended. Instead of simply reading about them, players interact with their history and work through the engineering problems they faced.

Historical information is clearly separated from fictional storytelling. Every transmission is labelled either "HISTORICAL RECORD" or "IMAGINED TRANSMISSION" to avoid confusing creative elements with actual mission data.

The pixel-art environment, animations, music and sound effects are generated within the browser using code. No external audio or image files are used for these elements.

Tools and technologies:

  • JavaScript
  • React 19
  • Vite
  • HTML Canvas 2D for the pixel-art environment
  • Web Audio API for procedural music and sound effects
  • NASA Image and Video Library API for mission imagery
  • Oxlint for code linting

The project was developed with attention to historical accuracy, accessibility, usability and privacy.

Mission information is supported by NASA sources, and historical records are distinguished from fictional transmissions. Keyboard controls, dialog focus handling and reduced-motion support were considered to make the experience more accessible.

The interface is designed to work on both desktop and mobile devices. Player names and generated Keeper's Cards remain in the browser and are not sent to an external server.

The use of Super Intelligence in development, including code, text and audio, is disclosed in the submission.
